experiment: Phase 2 — reasoning-derived claim windows (family votes height, obligations vote width)

design.window_center: weighted average of family-voted preferred heights
design.rationale: Each height is a loosely-justified region where the family's mathematical objects naturally live. de_branges → first eigenvalue cluster region. random_matrix → GUE-active high-T region. The rationales are illustrative not rigorous; the value is that they make Odlyzko grading depend on family choice, not on hash bytes.

honest_findings: Hyperloop has the WORST wrongness rate of the three (13.33% vs baseline 8.75%, klein 11.25%) — its bias toward checkable families concentrates candidates in explicit_formula/xi_function/hardy_z, all of which have preferred heights (30/40/50) near low-T zero clusters where any non-trivial window straddles a zero.

Hyperloop still wins external Odlyzko (+0.1088 vs klein, +0.0837 vs baseline) because rejecting 20 untestable candidates outweighs being slightly more wrong on average. The win is structural (less noise), still not predictive (less accurate).
Family-choice signal is now real: xi_function in baseline had 0/33 contradictions; same family in klein got 4/33. Same family, different mixing perturbations → different contradiction rates.
geometric_visualization (preferred height 80, far from low-T zero density) had 25% contradiction in baseline but 0% in klein — small sample (12 candidates) so this is noisy but suggestive.
what_phase2_does_NOT_show: The system is NOT learning from contradictions. A claim getting falsified produces no feedback that propagates back to Agent A — a deeper-orbit candidate could re-claim the same window next round.

The 'reasoning' here is heuristic: heights were chosen by the implementer to be physically plausible, not derived from the candidate's actual computed evidence (operator spectrum, prime distribution, etc.).
Hyperloop wins external mean while losing on wrongness rate — this means it's still optimizing for the wrong metric (untestability avoidance), not for empirical accuracy.
what_phase2_DOES_show: When claim windows depend on candidate properties, the Odlyzko benchmark differentiates between families by their actual contradiction rate, not just by their family-bonus accounting. This is the first time the system's design choices show up as different empirical accuracy footprints.

Klein topology adds cross-family candidates that systematically contradict more often — its K-novelty surface_return artifacts mix surface×depth pairs that produce 'reasoning' windows neither lane would have chosen alone, with predictably worse results on tight low-T windows.
next_phases: Phase 3: replace lean_bridge mock backend with real AXLE Lean kernel. Currently sorry-filled skeletons trivially pass mock verification.

Phase 4: when Odlyzko falsifies a claim, propagate the falsification back into dead_end_library. Then a candidate that picked a contradicted window pays a campaign-level cost, and Agent A learns to bias hypothesis generation away from height regions where its families produce contradictions.

Phase 5: derive family preferred heights from the candidate's actual computed evidence (e.g. for de_branges, parse the candidate's operator spectrum and pick a window near a real eigenvalue), not from a fixed table the implementer wrote.
